You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 9225b337072a10bf9b09df8bf281437488dd8a26 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Rob Clark <robdclark@chromium.org>
Date: Fri, 4 Mar 2022 12:21:45 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] drm/msm: Fix dirtyfb refcounting

refcount_t complains about 0->1 transitions, which isn't *quite* what we
wanted.  So use dirtyfb==1 to mean that the fb is not connected to any
output that requires dirtyfb flushing, so that we can keep the underflow
and overflow checking.

Fixes: 9e4dde28e9cd ("drm/msm: Avoid dirtyfb stalls on video mode displays (v2)")
Signed-off-by: Rob Clark <robdclark@chromium.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220304202146.845566-1-robdclark@gmail.com

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_fb.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_fb.c
index 96b379a08327..7137492fe78e 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_fb.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_fb.c
@@ -37,7 +37,7 @@ static int msm_framebuffer_dirtyfb(struct drm_framebuffer *fb,
 	/* If this fb is not used on any display requiring pixel data to be
 	 * flushed, then skip dirtyfb
 	 */
-	if (refcount_read(&msm_fb->dirtyfb) == 0)
+	if (refcount_read(&msm_fb->dirtyfb) == 1)
 		return 0;
 
 	return drm_atomic_helper_dirtyfb(fb, file_priv, flags, color,
@@ -221,6 +221,8 @@ static struct drm_framebuffer *msm_framebuffer_init(struct drm_device *dev,
 		goto fail;
 	}
 
+	refcount_set(&msm_fb->dirtyfb, 1);
+
 	drm_dbg_state(dev, "create: FB ID: %d (%p)", fb->base.id, fb);
 
 	return fb;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_fb.c`**
   - **Line Change**: The condition checking the reference count of `dirtyfb` was modified from `if (refcount_read(&msm_fb->dirtyfb) == 0)` to `if (refcount_read(&msm_fb->dirtyfb) == 1)`. This change alters the logic to skip the dirty framebuffer operation if the reference count is exactly 1, instead of 0.
   - **New Line Added**: A new line `refcount_set(&msm_fb->dirtyfb, 1);` was added in the `msm_framebuffer_init` function to initialize the `dirtyfb` reference count to 1 when a framebuffer is created.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in the condition for skipping the dirty framebuffer operation directly relates to the initialization of the `dirtyfb` reference count. By setting the reference count to 1 upon framebuffer initialization, the code ensures that the framebuffer is treated as not requiring dirty flushing when it is first created. This change addresses the issue of improper reference counting transitions (from 0 to 1), which was causing problems in the previous implementation. The overall goal of these modifications is to improve the handling of dirty framebuffer operations and prevent potential stalls in video mode displays.
